```{r}
dir <- './HmscOutputs'
pattern <- '2026-02-10'
make_VP_effect_sizes <- function(dir,pattern){
  pattern2match <- pattern
  
  matching_folders <- list.dirs(dir, recursive = FALSE, full.names = F)
  matching_folders <- matching_folders[grepl(pattern2match, basename(matching_folders))]
  model <- matching_folders[1]
  
  outputs <- lapply(matching_folders,function(model){
    # read objects
    MF <- readRDS(file.path(dir,
                            model,
                            'Results',
                            sprintf('%sMF.rds',
                                    model)))
    VP <- readRDS(file.path(dir,
                            model,
                            'Results',
                            sprintf('%sVP.rds',
                                    model)))
    effect_sizes <- read_excel(file.path(dir,
                                         model,
                                         'Results',
                                         sprintf('%sparameter_estimates_Beta_.xlsx',model)),
                               sheet = "Posterior mean")
    effect_sigs <- read_excel(file.path(dir,
                                        model,
                                        'Results',
                                        sprintf('%sparameter_estimates_Beta_.xlsx',model)),
                              sheet = "Pr(x>0)")
    
    load(file.path(dir,
                   model,
                   'Models/Fitted',
                   sprintf('HPC_samples_0250_thin_100_chains_4.Rdata')))
    m <- fitted_model$posteriors
    # get the atlas used
    X <- m$XData
    atlas <- unique(sapply(strsplit(rownames(X),'_'),'[',2))
    # get number of occurrences in that atlas
    if(!length(atlas)==1){
      stop()
    }
    occs <- data.frame(occs = colSums(m$Y,na.rm=T),
                       atlas = atlas)
    row.names(occs) <- colnames(m$Y)
    # get the trait date
    Tr <- m$TrData
    #transpose VP
    df <-VP$vals # get vals
    df <- as.data.frame(t(df)) # transpose into dataframe
    
    # merge VP with species info
    # 1. Prepare metrics and relative df first
    metrics <- data.frame(tjur = MF$TjurR2, auc = MF$AUC, row.names = m$spNames)
    df_rel <- metrics$tjur * df
    
    # 2. The main pipe, adding the scaled VPs 
    TrOccsTjurVP <- Tr %>%
      rownames_to_column("species") %>%
      inner_join(rownames_to_column(occs, "species"), by = "species") %>%
      inner_join(rownames_to_column(metrics, "species"), by = "species") %>%
      inner_join(rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(df_rel), "species"), by = "species") %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = c(tmean_year, prec_year, hh, `Random: site`,
                 starts_with("perc_")),   
        names_to = "environmental_variable",
        values_to = "VP_scaled_by_Tjur"
      )
    
    # 1. Pivot Effect Sizes to long format
    long_effects <- effect_sizes %>%
      select(-`(Intercept)`) %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = -Species, names_to = "environmental_variable", values_to = "effect_size") %>%
      rename(species = Species)
    
    # 2. Pivot Significance to long format
    long_sigs <- effect_sigs %>%
      select(-`(Intercept)`) %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = -Species, names_to = "environmental_variable", values_to = "sig_val") %>%
      rename(species = Species)
    
    # 3. Join, Mask, and Merge with your main data
    final_df <- long_effects %>%
      left_join(long_sigs, by = c("species", "environmental_variable")) %>%
      # Apply the mask: Keep only if sig <= 0.05 OR sig >= 0.95
      mutate(effect_size = ifelse(sig_val > 0.05 & sig_val < 0.95, NA, effect_size)) %>%
      select(-sig_val)
    # Join to your previous master table (assuming row names are Species)
    
    combined <- TrOccsTjurVP %>% 
      left_join(final_df,by=c("species","environmental_variable"))
    
    combined
    # adding effect sizes 
  })
  merged <- do.call(rbind,outputs)
  return(merged)
}
df <- make_VP_effect_sizes(dir,pattern)

# 1. Calculate the "Global Yardstick" parameters
# We use a separate temporary object to calculate the scaling factors
scaling_factors <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(effect_size)) %>%
  group_by(environmental_variable) %>%
  summarise(
    global_mean = mean(effect_size, na.rm = TRUE),
    global_sd = sd(effect_size, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# 2. Join back to the original dataframe and calculate the score
df_final <- df %>%
  left_join(scaling_factors, by = "environmental_variable") %>%
  mutate(
    # Only calculates for rows where effect_size and global_sd exist
    std_effect_size = (effect_size - global_mean) / global_sd
  )

# 3. Quick cleanup: View a few rows of the result
# We keep the NAs in the original columns but have the new scaled column
head(df_final)
df_final[df_final$species=='Picus_viridis','std_effect_size']
df <- df_final
species_vp_effect_plots <- function(df, species, english_name, remove_site = TRUE){
  subset <- df[df$species == species,]
  
  if(remove_site == TRUE) {
    subset <- subset[subset$environmental_variable != "Random: site",]
  }
  
  base_colors <- c(
    "Temperature"                  = "red",
    "Precipitation"                = "blue",
    "Land-use heterogeneity"       = "pink",
    "Urban (% coverage)"           = "grey",
    "Cropland (% coverage)"        = "yellow3",
    "Pasture (% coverage)"         = "orange",
    "Forest (% coverage)"          = "darkgreen",
    "Grass/Shrubland (% coverage)" = "lightgreen"
  )
  
  # --- STEP 1: CALCULATE SCALING ---
  # We use std_effect_size now since that's what we standardized
  max_vp <- max(subset$VP_scaled_by_Tjur, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Use the absolute max so the scale covers both positive and negative effects
  max_effect <- max(abs(subset$std_effect_size), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Avoid division by zero if max_effect is 0
  coeff <- if(max_effect == 0) 1 else (max_vp / max_effect)
  
  subset_clean <- subset %>%
    mutate(
      environmental_variable = case_match(environmental_variable,
                                          "tmean_year"       ~ "Temperature",
                                          "prec_year"        ~ "Precipitation",
                                          "hh"               ~ "Land-use heterogeneity",
                                          "perc_urban"       ~ "Urban (% coverage)",
                                          "perc_cropland"    ~ "Cropland (% coverage)",
                                          "perc_pasture"     ~ "Pasture (% coverage)",
                                          "perc_forest"      ~ "Forest (% coverage)",
                                          "perc_grass_shrub" ~ "Grass/Shrubland (% coverage)",
                                          .default = environmental_variable),
      environmental_variable = factor(environmental_variable, levels = names(base_colors)),
      atlas = factor(atlas),
      # Transform the data point to fit the R2 scale (0 to max_vp)
      std_effect_scaled = std_effect_size * coeff
    )
  
  ggplot(data = subset_clean, aes(x = environmental_variable)) +
    # Bars for Variance (Primary Axis)
    geom_bar(aes(y = VP_scaled_by_Tjur, alpha = atlas, fill = environmental_variable), 
             stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
    
    # Horizontal line at 0 for the secondary axis
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
    
    # Points for Standardized Effect Sizes (Mapped via the scaled column)
    geom_point(aes(y = std_effect_scaled, group = atlas), 
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
               color = "black", shape = 18, size = 3) +
    
    # --- STEP 2: DUAL AXIS ---
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = "Absolute variance explained (R²)",
      labels = scales::percent,
      # The sec_axis formula must be the INVERSE of the data transformation
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / coeff, name = "Standardized Effect Size (Relative to Community)")
    ) +
    
    scale_fill_manual(values = base_colors, guide = "none") +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c("1" = 0.4, "2" = 0.7, "3" = 1.0), 
                       name = "Atlas Period",
                       labels = c("1970s", "1990s", "2010s")) +
    labs(title = english_name, 
         subtitle = "Bars = Variance Explained (Primary) | Diamonds = Std. Effect Size (Secondary)", 
         x = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
          legend.position = "top",
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
species_vp_effect_plots(df_final,'Picus_viridis','Green woodpecker',remove_site = T)

species_vp_effect_plots(df_final,'Haematopus_ostralegus','Eurasian oystercatcher',remove_site = T)
```

```{r}
### TIMELINE 
# Prepare the summary data
timeline_data <- df_final %>%
  filter(!is.na(std_effect_size)) %>%
  # Define direction based on the standardized effect
  mutate(effect_direction = ifelse(std_effect_size > 0, "Positive", "Negative")) %>%
  group_by(atlas, environmental_variable, effect_direction) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_effect_abs = mean(abs(std_effect_size), na.rm = TRUE), # Width (absolute magnitude)
    n_species      = n(),                                     # Height
    .groups        = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  # Convert n_species to negative values for the "Negative" direction rows
  mutate(y_end = ifelse(effect_direction == "Negative", -n_species, n_species))

# Define your base colors from before
base_colors <- c(
  "Temperature"                  = "red",
  "Precipitation"                = "blue",
  "Land-use heterogeneity"       = "pink",
  "Urban (% coverage)"           = "grey",
  "Cropland (% coverage)"        = "yellow3",
  "Pasture (% coverage)"         = "orange",
  "Forest (% coverage)"          = "darkgreen",
  "Grass/Shrubland (% coverage)" = "lightgreen"
)

unique(timeline_data$environmental_variable)
# Create a numeric X position for each variable
timeline_data <- timeline_data %>%
    mutate(
      env_variable = case_match(environmental_variable,
                                          "tmean_year"       ~ "Temperature",
                                          "prec_year"        ~ "Precipitation",
                                          "hh"               ~ "Land-use heterogeneity",
                                          "perc_urban"       ~ "Urban (% coverage)",
                                          "perc_cropland"    ~ "Cropland (% coverage)",
                                          "perc_pasture"     ~ "Pasture (% coverage)",
                                          "perc_forest"      ~ "Forest (% coverage)",
                                          "perc_grass_shrub" ~ "Grass/Shrubland (% coverage)",
                                          .default = environmental_variable),
    # Ensure variables are factors so we can convert them to numbers
    env_factor = factor(env_variable, levels = names(base_colors)),
    env_num    = as.numeric(env_factor),
    
    # Base X is the atlas (1, 2, or 3). 
    # We add a tiny offset based on the variable so they fan out side-by-side.
    x_pos = as.numeric(atlas) + (env_num - mean(1:8)) * 0.1
  )

ggplot(timeline_data) +
  # Baseline representing the community average
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Arrows: Height = Number of Species, Width = Effect Size
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = x_pos, 
      xend = x_pos,
      y = 0, 
      yend = y_end,
      color = env_variable,
      linewidth = avg_effect_abs
    ),
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  
  # Scale width to represent the magnitude of the effect
  scale_linewidth_continuous(
    range = c(0.1, 5), 
    name = "Avg. Effect Size (Magnitude)"
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = base_colors, name = "Variable") +
  
  # Y-axis represents the number of species
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Number of Species (Negative vs. Positive Responses)",
    breaks = seq(-70, 70, by = 10),
    labels = abs # Display as positive numbers on both sides
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1, 2, 3),
    labels = c("Atlas 1\n(1970s)", "Atlas 2\n(1990s)", "Atlas 3\n(2010s)")
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Community Response Trends",
    subtitle = "Height = Species Count | Thickness = Mean Standardized Effect Size"
  )
```

```{r}
# Calculate temporal instability per species, per variable
temporal_instability <- df_final %>%
  # Remove NAs to ensure clean calculations
  filter(!is.na(std_effect_size)) %>%
  
  # Group by species and the environmental driver
  group_by(species, environmental_variable) %>%
  
  summarise(
    n_atlases = n_distinct(atlas),
    
    # The baseline: What is the average response across all time?
    mean_effect = mean(std_effect_size, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # THE METRIC: How much does that response bounce around between the 70s, 90s, and 2010s?
    effect_sd = sd(std_effect_size, na.rm = TRUE), 
    
    # Let's also grab the actual trajectory (Atlas 3 value minus Atlas 1 value)
    # This tells us the absolute direction of the shift
    shift_direction = std_effect_size[atlas == max(as.numeric(atlas))] - 
                      std_effect_size[atlas == min(as.numeric(atlas))],
    
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # We can only calculate SD if the species was modeled in at least 2 atlases
  filter(n_atlases > 1) %>%
  
  # Sort to put the most "unstable" relationships at the top
  arrange(desc(effect_sd))

# View the top 10 most shifting relationships
head(temporal_instability[temporal_instability$n_atlases==3,], 10)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Calculate Instability with NA = 0
instability_df <- df_final %>%
  # Replace NAs in the standardized column with 0
  mutate(std_effect_fixed = replace_na(std_effect_size, 0)) %>%
  
  group_by(species, environmental_variable) %>%
  summarise(
    instability_score = sd(std_effect_fixed, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_sens      = mean(std_effect_fixed, na.rm = TRUE),
    atlas_1_val    = std_effect_fixed[atlas == "1"],
    atlas_3_val    = std_effect_fixed[atlas == "3"],
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  # Calculate the absolute shift from start to finish
  mutate(net_shift = atlas_3_val - atlas_1_val)

# Identify the "Top Shifters" (most unstable species-environment pairs)
top_shifters <- instability_df %>%
  arrange(desc(instability_score)) %>%
  head(20)


# Filter for one variable to keep it clean (e.g., Temperature)
plot_data <- df_final %>%
  mutate(std_effect_fixed = replace_na(std_effect_size, 0)) %>%
  filter(environmental_variable == "tmean_year") %>%
  # Filter for species that have high instability in Temperature
  semi_join(instability_df %>% 
              filter(environmental_variable == "tmean_year") %>% 
              top_n(10, instability_score), 
            by = "species")

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = atlas, y = std_effect_fixed, group = species, color = species)) +
  # Draw a horizontal line at 0 (the "Average Bird" baseline)
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # Draw the trajectories
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  
  # Add labels to the ends of the lines
  geom_text(data = plot_data %>% filter(atlas == "3"), 
            aes(label = species), 
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5, fontface = "italic") +
  
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("1970s", "1990s", "2010s"), expand = c(0, 0.5)) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Niche Shifters: Temperature",
    subtitle = "Standardized Sensitivity across three Atlas periods (NA = 0)",
    y = "Sensitivity (Standard Deviations from Mean)",
    x = "Atlas Period"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# Plotting the Instability Score for all species across all variables
ggplot(instability_df, # Show only meaningful shifts
       aes(x = environmental_variable, y = species, fill = instability_score)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "red", name = "Instability (SD)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6)) + # Small text for long species lists
  labs(title = "Community-Wide Niche Instability",
       subtitle = "Red indicates species whose environmental relationship shifted drastically over time")
```
